newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine privatisation fund seeks new invest rules.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine privatisation fund seeks new invest rules.

text.p: Ukraine's State Property Fund is preparing a law to govern the sale of shares in large firms to strategic investors after parliament torpedoed its original plans, the fund's chairman Yuri Yekhanurov said on Thursday.
Parliament halted privatisation of more than 200 government-designated enterprises last month, saying there were no rules to oversee the process.

"We are working on a new law ordered by parliament, which in November halted tenders for strategic investment because it said there were not enough regulations for the process," Yekhanurov told a news conference.
The Ukrainian government had selected the companies for strategic investent to try to attract foreign funds.
Investors buying into the enterprises were required to provide money to modernise facilities.
Ukraine has attracted only $1.2 billion in foreign investment since independence in 1991.
The Fund managed to sell shares in six enterprises to strategic investors before parliament halted the process.
Yekhanurov said the SPF would continue taking small steps to keep the privatisation process going for the 200-plus enterprises until the law was accepted.
